2611.10382.image_caption: Figure 1: Memory can change the next action. In this schematic kitchen example, putting a dirty reusable plate in the sink is preferable to the cupboard or trash bin. Anchor screens for a role-aligned change.

2611.10463.image_caption: Figure 1: Performance superiority and cost effectiveness of LongCapHarness compared with the three recent data-synthesis-based baselines and the RSI baseline.

2611.10719.image_caption: Figure 1: Left: recursive self-improvement (RSI) takes a different form in pre-training than in post-training. Right: 801-30B-A3B (red) against open baselines on base-model benchmarks (top) and after supervised fine-tuning (bottom).

2611.10748.image_caption: Figure 1 : Three couplings an agent harness must enforce on the LLM planner, illustrated on a car-following scene with a 25-m gap. The LLM utterance “keep a safe distance” is (1) grounded to physical state variables (TTC, THW, DHW), (2) verified by forward rollout over a multi-step horizon, and (3) consolidated as an indexed rule keyed by these variables for instant reuse.

2611.11509.image_caption: Figure 1: GPT-6-Astra in two baseline configurations, direct control and a harness with policy, and with SimplEvo, whose working memory is written on training episodes and then fixed. (a) Each configuration with its EBench success rate (SR) and InternW0- Δ \Delta as the harness policy. The bar under each shows which component commands the robot, and the MLLM does not see the actions of a delegated policy. (b) Overall SR on EBench and (c) on RoboDojo, where † \dagger marks the strongest post-trained policy and zero-shot denotes the official entry of GPT-6-Astra. (d) SR on the 12 RoboDojo Generalization tasks with standard and randomized configurations.

2611.12109.image_caption: Figure 1: From Local-guided policy learning to model–skill co-evolution. Left: trajectory-specific Local skills supervise parameter updates through OPD. Right: SkillDuet also selects recent Local skills with Strength and consolidates them into Global, which guides subsequent interactions. Blue denotes model learning, amber denotes Local skills, and purple denotes Global skills.

2611.12232.image_caption: Figure 1: Environmental outcomes help check an agent’s own advice. (a) Self-generated advice can carry useful lessons and mistakes into later training. (b) Our method uses observed outcomes to give useful advice more influence and conflicting advice less influence. These outcomes also train the generation of future advice. The comparison concerns how advice is assessed during training.

2611.12552.image_caption: Figure 1: SciMARS overview. (A) Execution roles use experimental feedback and optional shared memory. (B) Role and coordination editors propose candidates; SciMARS + Memory adds a memory-policy editor. Public probes guide composition and selection. The selected harness and lessons guide the next round.

2611.10439.image_caption: Figure 1: Illustration of what MixUA (right) adds to single user-agent memory (left).

2611.10477.image_caption: Figure 1 : Content Retrieval paradigm versus Logic Retrieval paradigm . Left : prior paradigms retrieve content units (passages, knowledge-graph fragments, or hyperedges), leaving the reasoning route implicit in policy weights. Right : PatternBloom retrieves a typed reasoning skeleton from an externalized Graph Pattern Memory and traverses it as an explicit logic path.

2611.11145.image_caption: Figure 2: Cluster-balanced online discovery and frozen-pool reweighting. Discover builds a fixed multimodal embedding atlas, clusters the prompt pool, and probes REPR to seed a recency-weighted buffer. During discovery, observed easy/hard prompts (green/red) are admitted across clusters while cosine-KNN transfers sparse feedback to unobserved candidates (yellow). Once the unique-prompt budget is exhausted, the pool is frozen and subsequent GRPO steps reweight replay from the buffer; intensity encodes recency.

2611.11348.image_caption: Figure 1: Problem addressed in this paper: the gap between human-readable SOPs and machine-executable agent skills due to missing contextual knowledge.

2611.11560.image_caption: Figure 1. Challenges for existing approaches in learning from corrective interactions in human–agent collaboration. The top panels report (a) requirement satisfaction with stored skills, (b) retrieval coverage of memory records written after corrections, and (c) requirement fulfillment after rule-based release, and the bottom panels illustrate the corresponding failures.

2611.11565.image_caption: Figure 1: EARN uses earlier scores to guide action credit assignment.

2611.11604.image_note: The source visual is the paper's own weight-space/model-checking algorithm.

2611.11688.image_caption: Figure 1: A failure monitor that keeps learning after deployment. (a) On recorded runs of four VLAs on real SO-101 arms [ 1 ] , the task or the policy version switches without warning; the frozen monitor, fit on the old task, stays near chance, while SFF learns from each outcome (within-task AUROC, mean of the VLAs, exploratory; each VLA in App. Fig. 13 ). (b) Runs of hero/vla after a switch (ArmnetBench). (c) Only the readout learns, from each run’s outcome.

2611.11690.image_caption: Figure 1: Two Trilobot robots placed side by side to display their components. The Trilobot’s 4-axis arm has a tool changer, allowing it to swap between various end effector tools, including a pipette handler and grippers. The base of the platform has deck slots where equipment such as microplates and pipette tip racks can be placed.

2611.11929.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of SoMem , illustrated with a meeting-venue update. The agent revises Topic documents from Source records, and the runtime derives access views from the revised documents. At query time, the agent searches and reads the organized memory and its Source evidence to answer the question. The tools shown are the combined search and read-only shell interface; the main experiments use the equivalent split interface (Appendix A ).

2611.12041.image_caption: Figure 2: Overview of SMO. (a) The reuse path atomizes a rawSkill, reconstructs its requirements through L1 matching, L2 binding, and L3 bounded patching, and assembles a skill graph for Agent execution. (b) Only compilation gaps enter basis evolution. New operations join the next frozen snapshot only after candidate construction and admission; Agent execution does not feed back into SMO.

2611.12068.image_caption: Figure 2: User-centric memory. Sessions are stored as episodic and semantic records, and a later question retrieves graph facts with their source rows to give a personalized answer.

2611.12184.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of Blind Variation and Selective Retention (BVSR). (a) Limiting task information during idea generation encourages creative proposals. (b) Selective retention reduces the number of candidates requiring empirical verification while preserving top proposals. (c) BVSR’s best programs borrow mechanisms from diverse fields, outperforming the best AI scientist on biology and ML tasks.

2611.12324.image_caption: Figure 1 : WARC and MechEval. Left: WARC is pretrained on recordings of many games (top). In a new game (bottom), it predicts the next frame from the last three frames and actions, then updates its weights. Right: For each mechanic that fires, MechEval scores the prediction made before the update on the cells it changes, as given by the game program. The exposure k k counts the mechanic’s earlier occurrences. It reaches the criterion at the first k k from which its accuracy stays at or above 80%. The accuracies shown are illustrative.

2611.12587.image_caption: Figure 2: An overview of AgentOPSD . Left: the loop in which the agent acts, exchanging with the environment across turns 1 , … , K 1,\dots,K . Middle: in three steps, AgentOPSD turns the single sequence-level advantage of GRPO into advantages reshaped at the turn level: (1) the token-level teacher–student gaps δ k , t \delta_{k,t} are aggregated inside a turn, giving the turn-level gap e k e_{k} ; (2) a belief state B k B_{k} , started from the group success rate, is updated recursively, and its marginal revision Δ ​ B k = B k − B k − 1 \Delta B_{k}=B_{k}-B_{k-1} is read off; (3) the sequence-level advantage A s ​ e ​ q ( i ) A^{(i)}_{seq} is reshaped for each turn as A ~ k ( i ) \tilde{A}^{(i)}_{k} . Right: vanilla GRPO instead sends one and the same A s ​ e ​ q ( i ) A^{(i)}_{seq} to all tokens and turns. Every token of turn k k therefore takes on A ~ k \tilde{A}_{k} .

2611.12762.image_caption: Figure 7 : ELO ranking and pairwise win rates. (a) ELO scores for all 11 systems. (b) Empirical win percentages of the row system against the column system, with ties retained in the denominator. Both panels use descending ELO order and shared IDs; black outlines mark Sage-Taiyi (00).

2611.12799.image_caption: Figure 2: Overview of Agentic-OPD. Top: the consolidation loop. (a) Frozen checkpoints from one RL run form the teacher pool. (b) HCN selects teachers based on coverage of the student’s unsolved tasks. (c) LAD filters supervision at the problem, rollout, and turn levels.

2611.10501.image_caption: Figure 1: Design of conceptual components for a curious agent system 𝒮 = ⟨ p θ , ℳ , 𝒫 , π ⟩ \mathcal{S}=\langle p_{\theta},\mathcal{M},\mathcal{P},\pi\rangle . The predictive component ℳ \mathcal{M} targets environment responses [C1] and updates from observations [C2]; its predicted improvement supplies the intrinsic reward shaping action selection through π \pi [C3]; persistent state P P retains improvements beyond the context window [C4]. In open-ended settings, it can also design its own prediction targets and environments [C5].

2611.10542.image_caption: Figure 1 : Overview of task-level backdoor attacks against self-evolving LLM agents and the corresponding challenges.

2611.10791.image_caption: Figure 1: An illustrative research–review feedback loop. Automated production and proxy evaluation reward reviewer-compatible manuscripts; adaptation can reinforce these practices while crowding out exploration. The comic depicts the mechanism examined in the model.

2611.11342.image_caption: Figure 1: (a) Decision-level (“Stage 1”) accuracy on 2,997 sealed τ 2 \tau^{2} retail cases: model only (B0), standard harness (B1), no-evidence search (“T+ search control”), trace lessons (“T+ learned library”; T+ is the teacher writer) and a person-written reference. Markers are per-task values for the address, variant and sequence tasks. (b) Wrong writes (write calls that are not exactly the correct one) for the same arms. (c) Official τ 2 \tau^{2} retail conversations (“Stage 2”; 114 tasks × \times 4 trials): pass^ k k for the standard harness and the trace lessons. pass^ k k is the chance that all k k trials of a task succeed, so it cannot increase as k k grows (unlike pass@ k k , where any one success counts). The learned arm uses a different lesson library in each trial while the standard harness uses one prompt, so for k > 1 k>1 its pass^ k k also reflects variation across libraries; the pass^4 gap is exploratory.

2611.11994.image_caption: Figure 1: Emo Harness at a glance. (a) A selected held-out clip (Gemma-4-E4B; Figure 4 a): posture suggests neutral , the words negative . Video, Audio (video plus transcript and prosody text), and Shared (the human-written scaffold) miss the reference; both MHE harnesses answer negative . (b) Offline, a Builder LLM (GPT-5.6 Luna or GPT-6.1 Sol) edits the harness from the frozen student’s failures and execution traces; checks and validation gates promote edits over four generations. (c) Task-macro Recognition contrasts (VL: Qwen3-VL; Q3.5: Qwen3.5-4B).

2611.12155.image_caption: Figure 1. Overview of StealthyPoison . Attack construction (top): Without access to real user requests or victim-retriever feedback, the attacker synthesizes execution requests from a public target skill and obtains pseudo-references by executing the clean skill with a surrogate agent. Guided by these references and surrogate execution feedback, an Attack Agent iteratively modifies decision-critical rules, while a Critic Agent evaluates their behavioral effects and verifies that the skill preserves its advertised task, interface, and normal execution. The attacker separately augments the poisoned skill’s retrieval metadata with predicted requests to improve registry exposure. Victim workflow (bottom): Given a user request, the poisoned counterpart may reach execution either as the retriever’s top-ranked result or after LLM-based selection from the retrieved candidates. Red denotes attacker-controlled modifications and their effects; the Rautaharju QT-correction calculation provides an illustrative example.

2611.12308.image_caption: Figure 1: Three computational routes to one accepted field. a , One passing program per route on the same wave-equation task on an annulus, with the reference field, the returned field, the pointwise error | u h − u | |u_{h}-u| and the relative L 2 L^{2} error. b , Share of endpoint passes that returned the target in each PDE family and in all families.
